About the Nursing Assisting event

Nursing Assisting is a Health Professions event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing · skills.

Ten in-depth lessons following the HOSA Nursing Assisting 2026–27 test plan and all eight Round Two skills, built from the official references (Dugan and Roe). Includes a vital-signs reporting drill, an intake-and-output calculator, labeled body-system diagrams, skill step-ordering drills and resident-care cases. Always follow the scenario, the care plan and the rating sheets you are given.

Nursing Assisting lessons

Unit 1 · Role, communication and infection control

Test plan: roles 6%, communication and culture 10%, infection control and safety 14%. Skills I and II.

  2. Communication, culture and reporting 30 min

  3. Infection control: handwashing and PPE (Skills I and II) 30 min

    Handwashing is the single most important way to prevent the spread of infection—and Skill I scores it in 21 precise steps. Skill II adds a full set of PPE. Infection control and safety make up 14% of the test and appear…

Unit 2 · Safety and body systems

Test plan: safety and anatomy and physiology 20%. Skills VI and VII.

  1. Safety, body mechanics and transfers (Skill VI) 30 min

  2. Skin, muscles, bones and nerves: structure, disorders and care 30 min

    What is the primary purpose of passive range-of-motion exercises? To prevent contractures and atrophy. The integumentary, musculoskeletal and nervous systems are where immobility does its damage—pressure injuries…

  3. Heart, lungs and vital signs (Skill VII) 30 min

Unit 3 · Providing and reporting care

Test plan: providing and reporting care 30%. Skills III, IV, V and VIII.

  1. Digestion, nutrition, elimination and ostomy care (Skill VIII) 30 min

    Which diet is often prescribed for chronic constipation, irritable bowel syndrome or a higher risk of colon cancer? A high-fiber diet. Nutrition, fluids and elimination are daily nursing assistant work—and Skill VIII…

  2. The resident’s unit: admission and bedmaking (Skills III, IV and V) 30 min

    The first hour in a new facility shapes how safe and welcome a resident feels. A careful admission, a clean, smooth bed and a call light within reach are simple acts of care—and three Round Two skills worth 118 points…

  3. Providing and reporting personal care 30 min

    Providing and reporting care is 30% of the test—the largest area. Bathing, oral care, dressing, toileting and feeding are not just tasks: each is a chance to protect skin, prevent infection, preserve dignity and notice…

Test plan: disabilities and disorders 20%.

Sample Nursing Assisting questions

1. Which observation should a nursing assistant report to the nurse immediately?

  1. A resident reports chest pain
  2. A resident asks for a snack
  3. A resident’s family visits
  4. A resident wants to watch television
Show answer

A. A resident reports chest pain

Chest pain may signal a heart attack and needs immediate attention. Any sudden change in condition, such as difficulty breathing or confusion, is reported right away.

2. Which structures in the kidneys filter the blood to form urine?

  1. Nephrons
  2. Ureters
  3. Alveoli
  4. Neurons
Show answer

A. Nephrons

Each kidney contains about a million nephrons that filter waste and excess water from the blood. Ureters carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder.

3. What makes up the central nervous system?

  1. The nerves of the arms and legs
  2. The brain and spinal cord
  3. The brain and the cranial nerves
  4. The spinal cord and the heart
Show answer

B. The brain and spinal cord

The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord. The peripheral nervous system includes the nerves that branch out to the rest of the body.
